In the matter of :
Anoop Singh Negi (Injured)
S/o Sh. Dilbar Singh Negi R/o 1247, Sect-3, Pushp Vihar, Delhi-110017 ........ Petitioner  Versus 1. Mahesh (Driver)
S/o Sh. Shiv Kumar R/o H.No.8/48, Khichipur, Delhi.
2. Shiv Kumar(Owner)
S/o Sh. Saadhuram,
R/o H. No.H.No.8/48, Khichipur, Delhi.
3. HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company ..... Respondents Date of institution : 09.01.2018 Final arguments heard : 21.08.2023, 12.10.2023 & 16.10.2023 Date of Award : 18.10.2023 AWAR D 1.

The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after Act) by the investigating officer of FIR No.440/2017 Police Station Ghazipur, Delhi.
2. The accident in the present case took place on 04.12.2017.

It is the case of the petitioner that on that day, he was going on his scooty bearing registration No. DL-12SF-7226 from his house to Ghaziabad, U.P. to attend a marriage reception and at around 6:15 PM, when he reached on the flyover, road No. 56, from Ghazipur to Anand Vihar, Delhi, then a car bearing registration No.
DL-2CAX-0870 (offending vehicle) being driven by its driver Respondent No.1 Mahesh at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner, came from behind and hit the scooty of the petitioner,
as a result of which, the petitioner fell down on road and sustained injuries.
It is further stated that the offending vehicle run away from the spot and petitioner had noted down the number of the offending vehicle.
It is further stated that after the accident, he was taken to Hospital.
3. On notice of the petition, all the respondents have filed their written statement.
Respondents no. 1 & 2 filed their separate written statement mentioning therein that they have falsely been implicated in the present case.

It is further stated that the driver of the scooty was coming at fast speed from Anoop Singh Negi vs Mahesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35331873/
1 the side of Ghazipur underpass towards Anand Vihar Ghazipur and due to imbalance, scooty of petitioner slipped and fell down.

It is further stated that the accident had taken place on 04.12.2017,
whereas the petitioner had given his statement on 05.12.2017.
It is further stated that respondent No. 1 is having valid and effective driving licence.
4. Respondent No. 3 / insurer had given legal offer to the petitioner, which was not accepted by the petitioner.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 08.02.2018 :-
(i) Whether Sh. Anoop Singh Negi suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 04.12.2017 at about 6.15 pm on flyover, Road No. 56, Ghazipur, Delhi, within jurisdiction of PS Ghazipur due to rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle bearing Registration No.DL-2CAX-0870 (Maruti Echo) driven by Respondent No.1 / Mahesh?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether petitioner is entitled to the compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

(OPP) 
(iii) Whether petitioner is entitled to interest on the Award Amount, if so, to what rate of interest and for which period?
(iv) Relief 6.

In order to establish his claim, petitioner Anoop Singh Negi has examined himself as PW-1 and relied upon following documents:-
 disability certificate Ex. PW1/2  certified copy of FIR and DAR are respectively Ex.
PW1/3 and  certified copy of RC of DL and insurance of offending vehicle are

Discharge summary and medical treatment record Ex. PW1/9  Copy of PAN card,
aadhar card, bank pass book and DL of petitioner are Ex. PW1/10 to 13 7.
The respondent side did not led any evidence.

8. I have heard Sh. Lakshit Kothari, counsel for petitioner and Sh. Shrey Mehta, counsel for R-3 /
insurer.
No one appeared on behalf of respondents No.1 & 2 to advance arguments.
I have perused the record.

9. The issues are decided as follows:-
Whether Sh. Anoop Singh Negi suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 04.12.2017 at about 6.15 pm on flyover, Road No. 56, Ghazipur, Delhi, within jurisdiction of PS Ghazipur due to rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle Anoop Singh Negi vs Mahesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35331873/
2 bearing Registration No.DL- 2CAX-0870 (Maruti Echo) driven by Respondent No.1 /
Mahesh? (OPP)
10.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
11. Now in this case, the petitioner Anoop Singh Negi is injured and witness of the accident.
In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1.
He stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has clearly deposed that on 04.12.2017, the driver of the offending car was driving in a negligent manner and at a very high speed and hit his scooty.
As a result, he sustained grievous injuries.
It is mentioned in the FIR by the petitioner that he had noted down the number of the offending vehicle and the same was DL-2CAX-0870 and driver had fled away from the spot.

In part VIII of DAR under the head of 'Apparent Contributory Circumstances'
IO has mentioned in column no. 64 that the offending vehicle was being driven 'carelessly'.

In the charge-sheet, it is mentioned that during investiagtion, notice under section 133 of M.V. Act was given to owner / R-2 and he produced R-1 / driver (his own son) and replied that R-1 was driving the offending vehicle at the relevant point of time.
The mechanical inspection reports of victim vehicle and offending vehicle show that accidental impact was present on the vehicles.
It is mentioned in the mechanical inspection of offending vehicle that there was no fresh damage present and the vehicle had been fully repaired and only slight scratch on front bumper was present.
The offending vehicle was seized on 09.12.2017 and hence mechanical inspection was conducted thereafater on 10.12.2017 and hence possibility of repair cannot be ruled out.
FIR was given with delay of one day, which is not fatal and there is no reason of false implcation of respondents No.1 and 2.
Further, petitioner was not cross-examined by them either.
No suggestion was given to PW1 that the accident did nto take place with the offending vehicle in question.
12. After investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the car.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

sentences.text: 13. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
14. Respondent no.1 and 2 the owner and driver of the offending vehicle did not lead any evidence to prove any contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

sentences.text: 15. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and for filing of charge-sheet, it is proved that the petitioner Anoop Singh Negi received grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 Mahesh, the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

ISSUE No.2 :
Whether petitioner is entitled to the compensation as prayed for, if so, to what amount and for which period?
16. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
17. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not resulting loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.

18. Now, in the present case, the injured has not averred to suggest that he remained hospitalized for any particular period of time and has merely stated that he remained under treatment at Batra Hospital from 26.02.2018 to 01.03.2018.
The medical document of JPN Trauma Centre shows that he was discharged on 05.12.20217 i.e. date of visit itself and it was a case of LAMA.

The bill of Ambey hospital Ghaziabad suggest that the petitioner was first taken to the said hospital on the date Anoop Singh Negi vs Mahesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35331873/
4 of accident but in the absence of any medical document, it cannot be inferred that he remained hospitalized there.
There is no such medical document to suggest that from 04.12.2017 (date of accident) till before treatment at Batra Hospital, petitioner remained hospitalized in any hospital.
None of the medical certificate of Batra Hospital suggest that the patient was admitted or remained hospitalized even for a day.

However, the casualty discharge note dated 23.12.2017 reflects that the petitioner was managed conservatively with cast application for both bony leg fracture and he had reported increasing pain in right lower limb and inability to move his toes.
There was no local swelling or signs of increasing pressure found on cast cut and examination.
His was a case of fracture distil 1/3rd tibia.
The medical certificates of Batra Hospital reflects that the petitioner was advised rest from 01.03.2018 to 06.07.2018( about 17 weeks).
The IPD final summary bill of 26.02.2018 reflects the date of admission is 26.02.2018 but no discharge date is mentioned.
The IPD final bill detail of 01.03.2018 reflects the date of admission is 26.02.2018 but no discharge date is mentioned.
One receipt dated 01.03.2018 of billing section of Batra hospital shows that the petitioner was given permission to leave the hospital.

19. Therefore on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows :-
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
20.

Petitioner has proved on record his medical bills Ex. PW1/9 (colly) to the tune of Rs.1,41,865/-
(29 serial number of summary of bill is double counting of bill number at serial number 30 and 33.
The total summary of bill dated 01.03.2018 is for a sum of Rs.1,03,816/- which was paid in 3 installments as per bills at serial number 30,33 & 34).
The bill at Sl no. 24 of summary bill dated 21.02.2018 is for a sum of Rs.1350/- and wrongly calculated as 1550 in summary of bills filed by petitioner.
One bill at page No. 57 of document Ex PW1/9 bearing no. 18-19CR/OP191871 dated 23.05.2018 for sum of Rs. 150/- is not mentioned in the summary of bills and now is being calculated.

The medical documents /bills of Batra Hospital shows name of sponsor 'Delhi Govt.
Health scheme' and clarification was sought from the petitioner.

He stated on oath during examination under section 165 Indian Evidence Act that no concession or benefit was given to him under DGEHS card of his father, despite the panel name being mentioned in the Batra Hospital documents.
Under this head, only original medical bills are reimbursed.
Hence, an amount of Rs.1,41,865/- is being awarded under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
21.
According to his affidavit, after the accident, petitioner was treated in various hospitals.
He has not specified the period of his total hospitalization but clearly mentioned that he remained admitted in Batra Hospital from 26.02.2018 to 01.03.2018.
Further, the medical documents of Batra Hospital also corroborates this fact.
Considering that medical documents reflect that fracture was sustained by the petitioner and he remained under bed rest on medical advice from the month of March till July, 2018.
I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.25,000/- to the petitioner under this head.

CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES Anoop Singh Negi vs Mahesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35331873/
5 22.
The petitioner has not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.8,000/- to petitioner for conveyance and Rs. 4,000/- as special diet charges.
23. Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment and he has not claimed anything under this head.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- as attendant charges.
24. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.22,000/- (8,000+4,000+10,000) under this head.
LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :

Counsel for petitioner has stated that petitioner was on bed for more than 17 weeks and has filed on record medical certificate in this regard and he lost monthly income during the months of treatment.
No suggestion was given to petitioner to dispute this fact.
From the medical documents available on record, it can be seen that the petitioner remained under treatment from 04.12.2017 to 06.07.2018.
It is further seen that petitioner has not proved his salary slip Ex.PW1/3 on record and the same does not bear any signature or is accompanied with any certificate under section 65B IEA.
These pay slips have been disputed by the insurance company and suggestion was given to petitioner in this regard that the bills are forged and fabricated.
The pay slips are of January, April and July 2017.
Even if these pay slips are taken on its face value, they are of period prior to the accident and do not reflect any reduced salary.
The employer of petitioner was never examined by him.

Petitioner has deposed in his cross-examination that he is working in Manon Pvt. Ltd. Gurgaon but even while saying so, he nowhere claims that after the accident, he was employed at any lessor salary.

It is pertinent here to mention that in part VIII of DAR, it is mentioned that petitioner is 10 th pass and doing private job of waiter at monthly salary of Rs. 13,000/- but no educational document or job related document is part of DAR and further it is not specified in the DAR as to whether the petitioner was working in Delhi and what was the name of the employer.
IO has mentioned in the DAR that victim is 10th class pass but no educational document has been placed on record.

It is relevant here to mention that in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A,
petitioner has claimed to be employed Sodexo Food Solutions India Pvt. Ltd at a salary Rs.14,000/-
per month but the printout of salary slip unsigned salary slip (one of the salary slip for month of April 2017 is signed by petitioner himself underneath), shows monthly net salary as Rs.12,000/- per month Rs.12,001, and Rs. 11,000/- respectively.

entities.text: Sodexo Food Solutions India Pvt. Ltd
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioner has not given anywhere the address of his employer to deduce about the place of employment and copy of unsigned salary slip shows the address of employer as that Mumbai whereas the petitioner is a resident of Delhi.

Hence,
clarifications were sought from the petitioner regarding the place of his employment and further Anoop Singh Negi vs Mahesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35331873/
6 also on the point of facility under DGEHS as reflected through the Batra Hospital document.

He gave statement in writing during examination under section 165 Indian Evidence Act and stated that he was working in Jam Nagar, Gujrat and not Delhi and further head office of his employer was situated in Mumbai.

It is relevant here to mention that in DAR itself, it is mentioned that petitioner was employed and during his cross-examination, this factum was not disputed and no serious dispute was raised regarding his working with Sodexo Food Solutions India Pvt. Ltd.

entities.text: Sodexo Food Solutions India Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is seen that no suggestion was given to petitioner to dispute his claim of salary as mentioned in his affidavit Ex.PW1/A where he has claimed to be earning Rs. 14,000/- per month but salary slips (of January,
April and July 2017), though disputed by Ld. Counsel for R-3 show the salary to be Rs.11,000/-
Rs.12,000/-.
No evidence has been led by R-3 to dispute the salary slips and further it is seen that at the time of tendering of salary slips as document Ex. PW1/3, no objection was taken as to the mode of proof.
Hence, it can be concluded that petitioner was earning Rs.12,000/- net salary at the time of accident.

26. Hence, considering the testimony of the PW1 and taking into the account the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, who had suffered fracture in his left hand elbow and other injuries and also considering that petitioner has averred that he was under medical treatment in Batra Hospital from 26.02.2018 to 01.03.2018 and further the medical certificates of Batra Hospital dated 06.07.2018 reflect that total bed rest was advised to petitioner for 17 weeks approximately i.e. till 30.06.2018 and keeping in mind the document of JPN Hospital reflecting that petitioner last reported in the hospital in February 2018 and keeping in mind the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it can be assumed that petitioner must have been incapaciated to work for around 6 months.
Hence, for the loss of income, an amount of Rs.72,000/- (12,000X6) is being awarded as compensation under this head.
FUTURE LOSS OF INCOME ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY 27.

Ld. Counsel for petitioner has not submitted anything to suggest that petitioner has suffered from loss of income or any change in job profile to his detriment on account of permanent disability (as per disability certificate Ex.PW1/2) suffered by him.
To the contrary, record shows that he has taken up another job and is gainfully employed.

No doctor was examined by him to show that 5%
disability to the left lower limb has rendered the petitioner unable to carry on his day to day life and activities as before.
Hence, the functional disability is taken as zero percent in the overall facts and circumstances.
No compensation is being awarded under this head.
LOSS OF AMENITIES 28.
Though no evidence has been led by the petitioner on this head, considering his young age, a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

29. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-

7  Conveyance, Special diet & Rs.22,000/-

Whether petitioner is entitled to interest on the Awarded Amount, if so, to what rate of interest and for which period?
30. Petitioner has pursued his case since the year 2018, even though order sheet reflects that he was not very diligent.

Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization, excluding the interest for the delayed period, as mentioned in the order dated 10.7.2018.
It was mentioned in the said order that "Accordingly, the petitioner shall not be entitled to interest since 08.02.2018 till commencement of the evidence".
The said order was never recalled or modified and attained finality and the same was reiterated vide order dated 18.03.2021 and again this order was never challenged by the petitioner.
Evidence was finally tendered only on 28.04.2023.
Hence interest since 08.02.2018 till 27.04.2023 is not payable by the insurance company on the award.
Hence, the period from 08.02.2018 till 27.04.2023 is to be excluded in calculation of the interest.

LIABILITY:
31.
Since the offending vehicle insured at the time of accident and the respondent No.3 i.e. HDFC ERGO GIC Limited is the Insurer.
Thus, the respondents No.3 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

RELIEF:
32.

In view of the findings on above points, I, as presiding officer of this Tribunal,
award a total compensation of Rs.2,71,000/- (rupees two lakhs seventy one thousand only) along with interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization, excluding the period of delay as above explained, in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.3 / insurer.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.

33. It is relevant here to mention that vide order dated 13.02.2020, cost of Rs. 5000/-
was imposed on the petitioner which was reduced to Rs.2000/- vide order dated Anoop Singh Negi vs Mahesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35331873/
8 27.09.2019 but further on 13.02.2020, petitioner was given an opportunity to make payment of the reduced cost on the said date itself and it was further mentioned in the said order that failing this, the order for reduction of the last date would be recalled.
Further cost was imposed on the petitioner on 08.11.2021.
Costs are to be deposited by the petitioner with DLSA.
Considering the default on the part of the petitioner in payment of cost, it is clarified that compensation amount would be disbursed only subject to furnishing of cost payment receipts.

FUTURE LOSS OF INCOME ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY 27.
Hence, the functional disability is taken as zero percent in the overall facts and circumstances.
No compensation is being awarded under this head.
